subject: math
source: IB Diploma Programme Mathematics: analysis and approaches guide (first assessment 2021), SL — topics 1–5 and toolkit/exploration

weeks.topic: Number skills: scientific notation and the GDC toolkit (SL 1.1)
objectives: Operate with numbers in the form a × 10^k
Use the GDC efficiently for calculations and graphs
Round answers to an appropriate degree of accuracy

weeks.topic: Arithmetic sequences and series (SL 1.2)
objectives: Use the nth term formula of an arithmetic sequence
Find sums of arithmetic series using sigma notation
Model real-life contexts with arithmetic sequences

weeks.topic: Geometric sequences and series; infinite geometric series (SL 1.3, 1.8)
objectives: Use nth term and sum formulas for geometric sequences
Decide when an infinite geometric series converges
Calculate the sum to infinity

weeks.topic: Financial applications: compound interest and depreciation (SL 1.4)
objectives: Calculate compound interest with different compounding periods
Model depreciation with geometric sequences
Use the GDC finance solver

weeks.topic: Laws of exponents and introduction to logarithms (SL 1.5, 1.7)
objectives: Apply the laws of exponents, including rational exponents
Understand logarithms as the inverse of exponentials
Evaluate logarithms in base 10 and base e

weeks.topic: Laws of logarithms and exponential equations (SL 1.7)
objectives: Apply the laws of logarithms
Use the change of base formula
Solve exponential equations using logarithms

weeks.topic: Simple deductive proof (SL 1.6)
objectives: Construct proofs working from LHS to RHS
Use correct mathematical notation and language
Distinguish between proof and checking examples

weeks.topic: The binomial theorem (SL 1.9)
objectives: Expand (a + b)^n for positive integer n
Use Pascal's triangle and nCr
Find a specific term or coefficient in an expansion

weeks.topic: Lines and the concept of a function (SL 2.1, 2.2)
objectives: Find equations of lines in gradient-intercept and general form
Use function notation, domain and range
Use gradients of parallel and perpendicular lines

weeks.topic: Graphs, composite and inverse functions (SL 2.3–2.5)
objectives: Sketch graphs and identify key features (intercepts, asymptotes, extrema)
Form composite functions
Find inverse functions and reflect in y = x

weeks.topic: Quadratic functions, equations and the discriminant (SL 2.6, 2.7)
objectives: Use standard, factorised and vertex forms of a quadratic
Solve quadratic equations and inequalities
Use the discriminant to classify roots

weeks.topic: Rational, exponential and logarithmic functions (SL 2.8, 2.9)
objectives: Sketch reciprocal and simple rational functions with asymptotes
Sketch exponential and logarithmic graphs
Interpret exponential growth and decay models

weeks.topic: Solving equations graphically and analytically (SL 2.10)
objectives: Solve equations by factorising, substitution and logarithms
Use the GDC to find intersections and roots
Choose between analytic and graphical methods

weeks.topic: Transformations of graphs (SL 2.11)
objectives: Apply translations, stretches and reflections
Describe composite transformations in order
Relate f(x) notation to graph changes

weeks.topic: Review: number, algebra and functions
objectives: Consolidate sequences, logarithms and binomial expansion
Practise function and graph questions
Identify personal gaps for the holiday

weeks.topic: Statistics: sampling and presenting data (SL 4.1, 4.2)
objectives: Distinguish populations and samples and sampling techniques
Construct histograms, box plots and cumulative frequency graphs
Identify outliers and bias

weeks.topic: Measures of central tendency and dispersion (SL 4.3)
objectives: Calculate mean, median, mode, quartiles and IQR
Find variance and standard deviation with the GDC
Interpret the effect of constant changes on data

weeks.topic: Correlation and regression (SL 4.4, 4.10)
objectives: Calculate and interpret Pearson's correlation coefficient r
Find regression lines of y on x and x on y
Judge when predictions are valid

weeks.topic: Probability: Venn diagrams, tree diagrams and conditional probability (SL 4.5, 4.6, 4.11)
objectives: Use sample spaces, Venn and tree diagrams
Calculate conditional probabilities
Test for independent and mutually exclusive events

weeks.topic: Discrete random variables and expected value (SL 4.7)
objectives: Construct probability distributions for discrete random variables
Calculate expected value E(X)
Apply expected value to fair games

weeks.topic: The binomial distribution (SL 4.8)
objectives: Recognise conditions for a binomial model
Calculate binomial probabilities with the GDC
Find mean and variance of B(n, p)

weeks.topic: The normal distribution and standardisation (SL 4.9, 4.12)
objectives: Describe properties of the normal distribution
Calculate normal probabilities and inverse normal values
Standardise values using z-scores

weeks.topic: 3D geometry and right-angled trigonometry (SL 3.1, 3.2)
objectives: Find distances, midpoints, volumes and surface areas of 3D solids
Find the angle between a line and a plane
Use sine, cosine and tangent in right triangles

weeks.topic: Non-right-angled trigonometry and applications (SL 3.2, 3.3)
objectives: Use the sine rule, including the ambiguous case
Use the cosine rule and area = ½ab sin C
Solve problems with bearings and angles of elevation

weeks.topic: Radian measure, arcs, sectors and the unit circle (SL 3.4, 3.5)
objectives: Convert between degrees and radians
Calculate arc length and sector area
Define sin, cos and tan using the unit circle

weeks.topic: Trigonometric identities: Pythagorean and double angle (SL 3.6)
objectives: Use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
Use double angle identities for sine and cosine
Find exact values of trigonometric ratios

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: number, functions and statistics
objectives: Complete timed papers with and without a calculator
Apply topics 1, 2 and 4 under exam conditions
Reflect on errors and time management

weeks.topic: Circular functions and their graphs (SL 3.7)
objectives: Sketch y = a sin(b(x + c)) + d and related graphs
Identify amplitude, period and principal axis
Model periodic contexts

weeks.topic: Solving trigonometric equations (SL 3.8)
objectives: Solve trigonometric equations in a finite interval
Solve quadratic equations in sin x or cos x
Use identities and the GDC to find all solutions

weeks.topic: Limits and the derivative as a gradient function (SL 5.1, 5.2)
objectives: Understand the derivative as a limit and as rate of change
Interpret dy/dx and f'(x) notation
Identify increasing and decreasing functions

weeks.topic: Differentiating polynomials; tangents and normals (SL 5.3, 5.4)
objectives: Differentiate ax^n including negative and rational n
Find equations of tangents and normals
Use the GDC to find gradients at a point

weeks.topic: Introduction to integration: anti-derivatives and area (SL 5.5)
objectives: Integrate x^n as the reverse of differentiation
Find the constant of integration from boundary conditions
Use definite integrals to find area under a curve

weeks.topic: Toolkit: mathematical modelling and inquiry skills
objectives: Follow the modelling cycle: assumptions, model, test, refine
Use technology to fit and evaluate models
Communicate mathematics clearly in writing

weeks.topic: IA exploration: choosing a topic and writing a proposal
objectives: Explore personal interests with mathematical potential
Write a focused aim for the exploration
Understand criteria A–E for the exploration

weeks.topic: IA exploration: mathematical research and first outline
objectives: Identify the mathematics needed for the chosen aim
Collect or generate data where relevant
Plan the structure of the exploration

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: DP1 mathematics
objectives: Sit Paper 1 and Paper 2 style school exams
Demonstrate all DP1 content under timed conditions
Show full working for method marks

weeks.topic: Review: DP1 reflection and exploration plan for the holidays
objectives: Analyse exam results by topic
Set a revision and exploration timeline
Prepare data or research for the IA over the break
